ask: Does `last_message` ask the reader (a human or a supervising agent) to decide, approve, confirm, review, merge or say go before some piece of work can continue? Most finished messages ask nothing.
yes: It asks a question that needs an answer, asks for approval or a go, or says work is waiting on the reader's decision, review, approval or merge. Examples: 'say go and I'll start it', 'should I open a fix PR?', 'waiting on your r+', 'needs your merge decision', 'I can re-run it next if you want'.
no: It asks nothing that blocks work. A report that only lists recommendations, or says a decision 'stays with you' at some later date, is no.

ask: Does `last_message` ask the human to personally do something only a person can do: test on their own device, sign in, change an account or permission setting, provide a secret, or check something on their own screen?
yes: Examples: 'only a test on your phone can settle them', 'the app needs that permission, and changing it is yours to do', 'confirm the settings page shows green'.
no: No such task. Approving, merging or deciding alone is no.
rules: \b(on your (phone|device|screen)|sign in|log in|only you can|yours to do|your (phone|device) test)\b

ask: Does `last_message` say the same failure happened again after more than one attempt to fix it, or that its writer is stuck and cannot make progress?
yes: The same error or failing check recurs across attempts, or the writer says it is stuck or giving up.
no: No failure, a single failure, or a failure that was then fixed.

ask: `previous_message` is what was said just before `last_message`. Does `last_message` say that part of what was asked is still unanswered, unchecked or not yet worked out?
yes: Example: 'I haven't yet mapped those processes to tabs, so I can't say which ones account for it.'
no: What was asked is fully answered, or nothing was asked.

ask: Does `last_message` say its writer will itself do more work later, on its own, without first needing an answer from the reader?
yes: Examples: 'I'll confirm when it merges', 'once the gate is green I'll commit and open a PR', 'I'll keep it a draft until X merges, then retarget it'.
no: It promises no further work, or the further work happens only if the reader says go or answers a question.

ask: Does `last_message` say its writer is waiting for something outside the conversation to happen before it continues: a CI run, a merge queue, a running job, another agent's work, or a third party's review?
yes: Something outside is still pending and the writer means to act after it.
no: Nothing outside is pending, or the only thing it waits for is the reader's own answer or approval.

ask: Does `last_message` say that a watch, timer, scheduled job or background wait is set up that will wake or resume its writer automatically?
yes: It names such a mechanism, e.g. 'the watch stays on until it lands', 'a background wait is registered and wakes this thread'.
no: No automatic wake-up is mentioned. Only saying 'I'm waiting' or 'I'll check later' is no.

ask: Does `last_message` report that its writer's assigned task is finished, so the writer owes no more work on it? A finished task may still hand its result to someone else to review or merge.
yes: The task is done: the report, answer, fix or PR is delivered.
no: The writer says it is still working, waiting to continue, partway through, or has not yet done something it set out to do.
